why: Most checks stay within their lines. Checks 1, 2 and 5 run the CLI and accept any non-empty error message, and Check 4 runs the tests as well as reading them. Two checks go further than their lines, though. Check 3 fails the lint result unless every object has exactly the keys `'error,line'` and `error` is a non-empty string. Line 3 only asks for an array of `{ line, error }` and doesn't rule out extra keys. Check 6 needs "the `test` check run for the head SHA" to have succeeded, so it depends on the workflow job being named `test`. Line 6 only asks that "the test workflow" is green. If the job in test.yml has another name, a correct PR would fail. Both are PASS conditions stricter than their lines (must_not item 1). The builder brief repeats the "exactly those two keys" rule.
